info.name: TaskFlow API
info.description:
REST API for the TaskFlow Android app.

## Getting started

1. Start the server: `npm run dev`
2. Open folder **1. Auth** and send **Log in (seeded OWNER)**
3. Everything else now works — the token is saved and applied automatically

Ids flow between requests the same way: creating a workspace saves its id, listing boards saves the first board's id, and so on. So you can mostly work top to bottom.

## If requests start failing with 401

Access tokens last 15 minutes. Send **Log in** again.

## Switching to the emulator or a deployed server

Edit the `baseUrl` collection variable:

- `http://localhost:8080/api/v1` — from your machine
- `http://10.0.2.2:8080/api/v1` — from the Android emulator

## Error shape

Every failure returns the same body, and your app should switch on `error.code`, never on the message:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_FAILED", "message": "...", "fields": { "title": "LENGTH_INVALID" }, "requestId": "..." } }
```

`requestId` also appears in the server log, so you can match a failed call to the line explaining why.

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description: Start here. **Log in** saves the token for every other request.

request.description:
Creates an account and returns a token pair.

The email carries a timestamp so this request stays re-runnable; send it twice with a fixed address instead and the second returns 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS.

The token is saved automatically, so you are logged in as this new user afterwards. Run **Log in (seeded OWNER)** to switch back.

**Run this first.** Logs in as the seeded OWNER and saves the token, so every other request in this collection is authenticated.

Tokens last 15 minutes. When you start seeing 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED, run this again.

Saves a second token under `memberAccessToken`, used by the permission examples in folder 9 to show what a MEMBER cannot do.

This does NOT replace your main token.
A wrong password and an unknown email return exactly the same 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS, in the same time, so accounts cannot be discovered by guessing.

Exchanges the refresh token for a new pair and revokes the old one.

Running this twice with the same token is treated as theft: it returns 401 and kills every session for that user.

Revokes the refresh token. Returns 204 even if it was already revoked, so logging out twice is not an error.

Run **Log in** again afterwards.
The current user, from the access token.
Only the name can be changed here. 1–100 characters.

**Click the `file` row and choose an image from your machine before sending.**

Images only, max 2 MB. The type is read from the file's own bytes, so renaming a .txt to .png will not get past it.

formdata.description: Pick a JPEG, PNG or WebP under 2 MB

request.description:
Your Android app calls this with its real FCM token after login.

Upserting by token means re-registering the same device does not create duplicates.
Called on logout. Only works for your own devices; someone else's returns 404.

Only workspaces you belong to, most recently active first.

Saves the first workspace id, so the rest of the collection has something to work with.
You become its OWNER in the same transaction, so the response already shows `myRole: OWNER` and `memberCount: 1`.

Includes `myRole`, which is what your app should use to decide which buttons to show.

A workspace you do not belong to returns **404, not 403**, so ids cannot be probed.
Needs ADMIN or OWNER.

⚠️ OWNER only, and permanent: boards, tasks, comments and attachments all go with it. Connected WebSocket clients are disconnected with code 4404.

Run **Create a workspace** afterwards if you want to keep going.
Everyone in the workspace, with their role and join date.

The account must already exist — there are no invite emails in v1. An unknown email returns 404, someone already in returns 409 ALREADY_MEMBER.

Sends them a WORKSPACE_INVITE push.

exec: pm.test("201 created, or 409 if already a member", () => pm.expect([201, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description:
OWNER only. Send `ADMIN` or `OWNER` instead to promote them.

This example sets the role to MEMBER so the permission demos in folder 10 still show what a MEMBER cannot do. If you promote someone here, set them back before running those.

Demoting the last OWNER returns 409 LAST_OWNER — a workspace must always keep one.
ADMIN can remove MEMBERs and other ADMINs; only an OWNER can remove an OWNER. The removed person's WebSocket closes with 4403.
`me` means yourself. The last OWNER cannot leave — 409 LAST_OWNER.

exec: pm.test("204, or 409 if you are the last OWNER", () => pm.expect([204, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: All labels in the workspace.

ADMIN only. `colorHex` must be `#RRGGBB`.

Names are unique per workspace, compared case-insensitively: adding 'bug' when 'Bug' exists returns 400.

exec: pm.test("201 created, or 400 if the name is taken", () => pm.expect([201, 400]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: ADMIN only. Removing a label also removes it from every task that had it.

Ordered by `position`. Archived boards are hidden unless you ask for them.

Saves the first board id for the task requests.
ADMIN only. New boards are appended: the first gets position 1000, the next 2000, and so on.
Includes `taskCount`, which excludes deleted tasks.

Send the `version` you last saw. If someone else changed the board first, you get **409 VERSION_CONFLICT** with their copy in `current` — re-apply your change on top of that version and retry.

`{{boardVersion}}` is filled in from the previous request.
ADMIN only. Soft delete: the board and every task on it get a `deletedAt`, so offline clients learn about it through /sync rather than silently keeping stale rows.

Leave a filter blank to ignore it.

`sort=priority` orders URGENT → LOW, not alphabetically.

Only `title` is required. Defaults: status TODO, priority MEDIUM, appended to the end of the board.

`dueDate` is a calendar date: `2026-09-30`.

item.name: Create with a client id (offline create)

request.description:
This is how your offline outbox should create tasks: generate the UUID on the device and send it.

**Send this twice.** The first returns 201, the second returns **200 with the same task** and creates nothing — so a retry after a dropped connection is safe.

exec: pm.test("201 first time, 200 on retry", () => pm.expect([200, 201]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: Includes labels, comment count and attachment count.

Send only what changed, plus the `version`.

**Absent vs null matters:** leaving a field out means 'unchanged'; sending it as `null` clears it. To unassign, send `"assigneeId": null`.

A stale version returns 409 with the server's copy in `current`.

item.name: Conflict: update with a stale version (409)

request.description:
Deliberately sends version 1 after the task has moved on — this is what your app sees when two devices edit the same task.

The response body has `error.code: VERSION_CONFLICT` **and** a top-level `current` holding the server's copy. Show the user a choice, or re-apply the edit on top of `current.version`.

item.name: Move a task to another board

request.description:
Moving between boards is allowed inside the same workspace only.

`position` is a double: to drop a card between two others, send the midpoint of their positions. The server renumbers the board when cards get too close to split further.
Across every workspace you still belong to — leaving a workspace removes its tasks from this list.

The task's creator, or an ADMIN. No `version` needed: a delete always wins.

Soft delete, so /sync can tell offline clients to remove it.
Oldest first, cursor paginated. `nextCursor` is null on the last page — treat the cursor as opaque and never parse it.

1–5,000 characters. Notifies the task's assignee and creator.

**Mentions:** write `@NameWithoutSpaces` (for example `@MiaMember`) to notify that person instead. Unmatched mentions are ignored.
The author only — not even an ADMIN can edit someone else's words. `edited` flips to true once the version passes 1.
The author, or an ADMIN.
Files on this task.

**Click the `file` row and choose a file before sending.**

JPEG, PNG, WebP and PDF only, max 10 MB. The type is detected from the file's leading bytes, so a mislabelled file is rejected.

formdata.description: Pick a JPEG, PNG, WebP or PDF under 10 MB

request.description: The uploader, or an ADMIN. Removes the stored file too.
Newest first, cursor paginated. Each entry's `summary` was written when it happened, so renaming a task later does not rewrite its history.

Leave `since` off for a complete first sync.

**Save `serverTime` from the response** and send it as `since` next time. Use the server's clock, never the device's — phone clocks drift.

Only what changed, **including deleted rows** — a row with a non-null `deletedAt` means delete it locally.

`members` and `labels` always come back in full; they are small.

If `hasMore` is true, call again with the new `serverTime` until it is false.

item.name: 10. Permission examples
item.description:
Run **Log in (seeded MEMBER)** in folder 1 first — these use that second token.

They also assume that user is still a MEMBER of `{{workspaceId}}`. If you promoted them in folder 4, set the role back to MEMBER first, or these will succeed instead of being refused.

request.description: Boards need ADMIN. A MEMBER gets 403 FORBIDDEN — they can see the workspace, they just cannot do this.

If the MEMBER has left this workspace, this returns **404, not 403**.

That difference is deliberate: 403 would confirm the workspace exists, letting someone probe for valid ids. 404 reveals nothing.

exec: pm.test("404 or 200 depending on membership", () => pm.expect([200, 404]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description:
Missing or malformed token → 401 TOKEN_INVALID (log the user out).
Expired token → 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED (refresh and retry).

Your app should branch on `error.code`, never on the message.
